data.title: Positioning — kadence
body: # Positioning — kadence
> **Superseded 2026-09-16 by [strategy.md](DOC-35).** Kept as history; where the two disagree, strategy.md wins.
- **Date:** 2026-09-04 (rewritten after the [positioning review](DOC-28))
- **Method:** Geoffrey Moore, *Crossing the Chasm*
- **Status:** working. Rests on Probe A data and on the market scan of September 2026; the bet on the value of history is waiting on Probe B
## What changed and why
The previous revision put sprint analytics in the headline: "we count what a point costs". The market scan of September 2026 showed that we were measuring the wrong axis.
| What was found | Consequence |
| Work in the repository has become mainstream: GitHub Spec Kit (38 integrations with agents), Beads, Backlog.md | The "tasks in files" category is taken. But **all three store mutable state** |

| Spec drift is an acknowledged ailment of the category: "static specs are not updated during implementation" | That is a problem of mutable state. Our append-only journal does not drift by construction |
| An agent loses context between sessions ("context amnesia") — a problem Beads named out loud | A real, fresh and acknowledged pain. Sprint analytics next to it looks secondary |
| "Having MCP is becoming a competitive requirement"; Backlog.md calls CLI agents *legacy* | "Without MCP" is no longer a slogan. Files are the foundation, MCP is an option |
**Decision: the main message is the shared context of a team's work and AI. The immutable journal is the mechanism that provides it. Velocity is a consequence, not the headline.**

The difference is fundamental. "We count velocity" is a promise to a manager once every two weeks. "You and your agent see the same thing" is a promise to a developer every day, and it is visible every time an agent starts a new session.
## Category

Not "git-native task tracker" — that is where Backlog.md, git-bug and git-issues are. Not "spec-driven development" — that is where GitHub with Spec Kit is, and we cannot compete with it using its own weapons.
**Category: the shared context of the work of a team and its AI agents in the repository.**

The difference from the neighbours is *what exactly* is stored. They store **state**: a task file, a row in a database, the current specification. We store **events**: what happened, when, and who did it. For us, state is a derivative that can be recomputed at any time.
## Value proposition
> **For** teams of 3–8 developers who work with AI agents and keep the work next to the code,
> **who need** the human and the agent to work from one context rather than assembling it anew each time,
> **kadence** —
> **is** a journal of the team's work in the repository,

> **which** keeps tasks, their full history and the time spent as immutable events next to the code: the context is not lost between sessions, does not conflict when branches are merged, and along the way shows what the work cost.
## Differentiation
> **Unlike** Spec Kit, Beads and Backlog.md, which store **mutable state** — and therefore drift, conflict, or hide history,
> **kadence** —

> **stores events**: the history cannot be rewritten, merging branches needs no manual sorting out, and from that same stream come the current state, the velocity, and the answer to the question "how did we get here".
| | Spec Kit | Beads | Backlog.md | kadence |
| Work lives in the repo | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| What is stored | static specs | state in SQLite | markdown files | **events** |
| Drift | present, acknowledged | state is mutable | state is mutable | **impossible by construction** |
| History of "how we got here" | no | partly | no | **that is the journal itself** |
| What it cost | no | no | no | **yes** |
| Conflicts on merge | present | binary DB | present | **none, measured** |
| MCP | yes | yes | yes | **as an optional package** |
## One sentence for the README
> **Your team and your agents work from one context — it lies in the repository and remembers what the code does not.**
## Name risk

The name collides with [Kadence WP](https://www.kadencewp.com/) — a WordPress site builder with 400 000+ installations. Organic search for the word "kadence" is closed to us, and part of the audience (web developers) expects a WP theme behind that word. Decision of 2026-09-04: we keep the name, because the npm name is already ours; the domain was planned as `kadence.tools`, but on 2026-09-13 `kadence.guru` was registered — the site lives there. Details and consequences are in the [visual direction](DOC-18), section 11.
## Stress test
| Question | Answer |
| Does the customer recognize themselves? | Yes — a team that already works with agents and has already lost context between sessions |
| Is the need proven? | **Partly.** "Context amnesia" has been named out loud by a competitor and by industry reviews — but not by us and not on our users. Probe B has still not been run |
| Does the category help? | Yes — it takes us out of the "whose board is better" comparison |
| Is the differentiation provable? | **Yes.** Append-only has been verified twice: our integration test and 8 396 other people's merges |

| Does it drive decisions? | Yes — and it has already changed them. `kadence context` was **removed** 2026-09-07: [Probe C](DOC-57) measured that `task show --json` already returns the task's whole history in 948 bytes regardless of project size. What remains is `kadence decision` and the optional MCP; ornamentation in the TUI ranks lower |
## What is deliberately absent here
- **"We give the agent context"** — the agent reads the repository anyway. We give **history and structure**, which are not in the code
- **"Without MCP" as a slogan** — in 2026 that reads as "behind the times", not as "simple". Files are the foundation, MCP is an option
- **Competing with Spec Kit** — it writes the specification, we remember what happened to it afterwards. These are different layers
- **The PM as a TUI user** — the PM works through an agent, and that is exactly why the agent needs a readable journal
- **Velocity in the headline** — it stays, but as a consequence of the journal, not as the reason to install the product
## What would make this positioning wrong

If it turns out that agents do perfectly well with `git log` and the code, and that teams do not feel a loss of context between sessions, the positioning falls. What then remains is sprint analytics for a narrow segment.

The cheapest check no longer costs a day of work — it costs nothing: `kadence task show KAD-1 --json` already exists. Give an agent a task with the journal and without it, and compare how much it asks again. Probe C showed that the answer became 948 bytes and does not grow with history; what it did not show is whether anyone needs the answer itself.
